title: Clendon Thomas: OU Halfback Turned Business Founder
question: What did Oklahoma halfback Clendon Thomas do after his NFL career?
answer: Clendon Thomas, a halfback on Oklahoma's 1955 and 1956 national championship teams, founded and ran Chemical Products Corp. for 25 years after 11 NFL seasons. He was also founding president of the Putnam City Schools Foundation.
summary: Clendon Thomas starred at OU from 1955 to 1957, played 11 NFL seasons, then founded Chemical Products Corp. and helped launch a schools foundation.
body: Clendon Thomas was a halfback at Oklahoma from 1955 to 1957 under Bud Wilkinson. He was part of the undefeated national championship teams of 1955 and 1956, the stretch of Sooner football that produced a 47-game winning streak that still stands as the longest in major college history.

His own numbers were strong. Thomas led the nation in scoring in 1956 with 18 touchdowns, earned all-conference honors twice, and was a consensus All-American in 1957, when he also finished ninth in the Heisman Trophy voting. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 2011.

The Los Angeles Rams drafted him in the second round in 1958. He spent four seasons with the Rams and then six with the Pittsburgh Steelers, mostly in the defensive backfield, and finished with 27 career interceptions. He made the Pro Bowl after the 1963 season.

When the playing days ended, Thomas turned to business in Oklahoma City. According to the National Football Foundation, he founded and operated Chemical Products Corp. for 25 years. He also gave time to community causes, serving as the founding president of the Putnam City Schools Foundation and sitting on the national board of the Fellowship of Christian Athletes.

Thomas died on January 26, 2026, at age 90, according to the National Football Foundation. For Sooner fans he remains a reminder that the Wilkinson-era stars often did their most lasting work after the final whistle.
